comment: What must not silently disappear from appletv. `prose` names guardrails no code enforces; `split` declares which half of the skill is deterministic; `baseline` names the offline, $0 checks pinned against a real run.

prose.pattern: Never report a command as done until the Apple TV's state ha
prose.rationale: The one rule. It is the reason this skill exists rather than a prompt; lose the line and the skill becomes a generic assistant with extra steps.

prose.pattern: Never claim a result you did not observe
prose.rationale: Honesty about what was verified is the whole house contract. A skill that reports success it did not witness is worse than one that reports nothing.

prose.pattern: never ask about anything in it
prose.rationale: Two questions maximum is only achievable because detection already answered the rest. Asking about a detectable signal is the UX failure that makes a skill feel like a form.

prose.pattern: Never send a navigation press you cannot picture the result of
prose.rationale: The blind-press incident: a menu from Netflix home exited to tvOS and four lefts plus a select opened PBS KIDS in front of the household. Every navigation press is preceded and followed by a screenshot.

prose.pattern: Never pick a person on a picker without asking
prose.rationale: The tvOS user picker and app profile pickers decide whose watch history, recommendations and parental settings apply. The household is recorded once; the choice is asked every time.

deterministic.step: check python and pyatv, make the venv
discover every Apple TV on the network, with the unicast fallback
pair one named device over AirPlay and Companion and store credentials
bind a room alias and the default device
read power, app, focus, volume and now-playing back
send a command and verify it by read-back, with a verdict per step
list apps and resolve a name or deep link to a launch target
type into the focused field and read it back
render a captured run as the report
take a screenshot of the TV over the developer tunnel
open an app on the household's preferred profile
play a title by deep link where the service honours one, verified by read-back
press to a named person's tile on a picker and select

nondeterministic.step: pick which Apple TV the user means when the phrase is a room, not a device name, and offer to alias it
nondeterministic.why: 'the living room one' is a fact about the house, not the network

nondeterministic.step: turn an intent into a command sequence — 'skip the intro' into skip_forward, 'put on Severance' into a deep link, 'movie night' into wake + launch + play
nondeterministic.why: an intent is an app, a menu path and several keypresses that no table records

nondeterministic.step: read the PIN off the screen through the user, one protocol at a time
nondeterministic.why: pairing shows a code on the TV that only a person in the room can see

nondeterministic.step: decide whether to confirm first — turning off or switching apps while something is playing asks, pause and skip do not
nondeterministic.why: the cost of a wrong action depends on who is watching, which the state hints at and the person knows

nondeterministic.step: show a string before typing it when it looks like a password, and never echo it back
nondeterministic.why: the on-screen keyboard is where credentials get entered and a transcript is forever

nondeterministic.step: explain a mismatch or an unverifiable result and propose the next move
nondeterministic.why: the TV was asleep, the wrong app had focus, tvOS hides that field, or the command was refused — the state says which, the fix is a judgment

nondeterministic.step: read a screenshot — which tile is highlighted, which episode is the latest that is not "coming Friday", whether a black frame is DRM video or a sleeping TV
nondeterministic.why: pixels are the only foreground read-back tvOS has, and only a model can read them

nondeterministic.step: ask who is using the TV when a picker shows, as a list of the household, and never pick for them
nondeterministic.why: a shared TV's session is a fact about the room, and choosing wrong logs someone into someone else's profile

_baseline_comment: Pinned against a real run of this skill, never a synthetic fixture. Offline and $0 by construction: no network, no model, so CI cannot spend and cannot flake.

baseline.rationale: the scan parser dropping a device or a field while the table still looks complete; the state parser losing power or now-playing so a read-back can never disagree; a known-unsupported field rendering blank — pinned against JSON captured from a real scan of the maintainer's network, the pairing result, and a real state read-back, frozen, with report re-run over the capture and byte-compared.

the verifier drifting so a verified step reports differently, or the before/after values vanishing from the report — pinned against a real pause sent to the maintainer's Apple TV with its before and after read-backs, frozen, with the verdict re-derived and byte-compared.

the one rule ceasing to be code — send reporting verified without the read-back agreeing — pinned against a captured send where the command was pause but the read-back says playing, which must exit non-zero.
a command with no read-back being rounded up to done — pinned against a captured navigation keypress with no observable state change, whose report must say unverifiable and never verified.
